# Research log: input search (generated by `tools/research_log.py` from the search ledgers)

Rules: `bench/PROTOCOL.md` section 6b. Every number here is a VALIDATION number (the 90 days before each fold's training end,
trained-on symbols). Test folds were not read by the search. Objective = mean over hourly h 1 / 6 / 24 and daily h 1 / 5 of
asset-equal sPL / sqrt(h), four folds; lower is better. Stages: `s1` = 500 steps on fold F3, `s2` = 1,500 steps on F1 + F3,
`full` = 1,500 steps on all four folds, then the paired block-bootstrap comparison with the incumbent. Promotion needs the 95 %
interval of the improvement above zero at two or more of the five (task, horizon) pairs and significantly worse at none.
All configs: size s (4 layers x 128), patch 16, same seed and the same training windows per fold, so differences come from inputs.

Wave 1 searched inputs available from the hourly archive for all 350 pool symbols. Wave 2 added inputs that need the 5-minute
archive (intra-hour realised variance and its downside share) plus peer and BTC-range inputs; it uses the 64 evaluation symbols
only (trained on the 47 seen ones), so its incumbent was retrained in that setting first and comparisons stay paired.

Wave 3 changed the objective to the validation rank IC of the median (mean over the five task-horizon pairs; the "validation
objective" column is minus that IC) and trained on grouped batches (32 origins x 32 symbols) so a within-origin correlation
loss on the median could be added (`ic10`, `ic30` = weight 0.1 / 0.3). Paired improvements in wave 3 are IC points x 100.
The promoted wave-3 config was then scored once on the unseen folds and did not confirm (`agent/LEADERBOARD.md`).
